correctness.rationale: The exact adjacency singular spaces are computed from the unsigned incidence matrix. Projector Schur squares yield a positive-semidefinite sum including the necessary collision correction for equal part sizes; the kernel intersection is solved separately for all six boundary regimes. A standalone rational checker reconstructs projectors independently and matches 1,131 matrix entries across nine graphs, with exact rank checks in all small cases. This finite evidence supports rather than replaces the proof.

originality.rationale: Primary sources establish the Schur identity, general exact algorithms and simple-spectrum rank bounds, but not the complete once-subdivided biclique two-parameter formula or kernel transition. The closest previous complete-graph subdivision and symmetric-design incidence results have different graph hypotheses, while path endpoints are already covered. No implication covering the full new statement was found in the inspected materials; residual risks are explicit.
residual_risks: A stronger general incidence-graph Schur-square theorem, particularly one stated via association schemes or spectral multiplicity algebras, may imply this specialization without naming the family.
Search coverage is necessarily incomplete; full text was read for relevant sections rather than every page of every cited work.
The very small path endpoints are known and cannot count toward originality.
No independent external scientific audit or literature certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly characterizes when a canonical incidence-graph operation produces positive-definite long-time quantum mixing, gives a sharp part-size threshold, resolves all six exceptional nullity and kernel regimes, and supplies a universal rational matrix formula. This structural classification is motivated by quantum transport rank rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical slice.
